analysis.title: Global Equity Strategy: 2027 Outlook: Finding Value in Growth
key_insights: GS expects the global equity bull market to continue in 2027 with positive returns but higher volatility, as slower nominal growth, lower bond yields, lower oil prices and de-rated valuations offset a sharp earnings slowdown.

2026 was driven by earnings. Returns were similar across regions, reversing the 2009-2025 pattern of US outperformance, and all equity markets de-rated. Earnings revisions were strong on tech earnings, higher oil prices boosting commodity earnings, and capex spill-over into HALO (heavy asset, low obsolescence) industries such as Industrials.
GS top-down 2027 EPS growth roughly halves or worse in every major region: US 36% to 11%, Europe about 18% to 7%, Japan 24% to 9%, Asia from close to 80% to under 30%.

Slower hyperscaler capex growth is the main drag on earnings growth for the AI infrastructure complex, including Industrials. Depreciation and interest costs are also rising. Consensus shows IT earnings growth slowing from about 90% to 45% and Communication Services from 34% to -5%.

Energy prices are expected to moderate. Consensus has Energy EPS growth going from 99% in 2026 to about -10% in 2027 and Basic Materials from 45% to 12%. Defensive sectors such as Healthcare are the exception to the broad slowdown.

Cost of capital stays elevated. GS rates strategists expect a modest tightening cycle and slow progress on cuts in 2027, credit strategists expect spreads to widen, and bond strategists see some relief in long-term yields. The Fed and ECB should move toward cuts in late 2027, and GS rates forecasts are more dovish than market pricing.
GS focuses on three areas: Growth, selective Defensives, and beneficiaries of lower oil prices and bond yields. It favors selective Defensives over a broad defensive shift.

Hyperscalers are the preferred growth expression. Their P/E has fallen to 19.7x, below the previous 20-year range and cheaper than Consumer Staples, and the premium of the largest US stocks over the other 495 has virtually closed. Balance sheets remain healthy on net debt/equity despite negative free cash flow at the biggest companies.

Global Technology trades at the 20th percentile of its 20-year P/E range and is now one of the cheapest sectors, similar to the Value factor. EM IT, dominated by a few chip stocks, is the cheapest it has been in 20 years. Value sits near the 90th percentile of its own range and is no longer as cheap relative to Growth.

Selective cyclical growth offers value in Semiconductors and some Consumer Cyclicals. Korea's memory sector is pricing a 70% cut to 2027 consensus earnings and trades at 0.7x 2028 P/B, against company statements of DRAM and HBM sold out until 2029. GS flags much higher risk and volatility.

Regional stance on risk-adjusted returns: overweight US and Japan, neutral Asia ex Japan and EM, underweight Europe. Forecast returns are highest in Asia and EM, but GS cites high concentration, 24.2% YTD volatility for MXAPJ, and higher momentum risk in Asia.

Europe is the clearest beneficiary of lower oil prices and gas prices through consumers, but lower oil also cuts European earnings growth. GS stays underweight because valuations have fallen less than elsewhere and risks are higher from government debt and a heavy political calendar.

Brent is forecast to fall from about $100/bbl at end-2026 to $78/bbl at end-2027, turning the energy-price impulse from a 0.4pp drag on global growth into a modest boost. Together with fading tariff effects and easing AI supply pressure, this should lower inflation.

Four risks, each two-sided: bond volatility (sovereign debt risk highest in Europe), oil volatility, weaker AI capex that could de-rate memory, chips and parts of Industrials, and narrow breadth and momentum concentration in the US and Asia. GS sees US large-cap tech as more defensive than Asian tech.

sector_views.rationale: P/E has fallen to 19.7x and the premium to the other 495 US stocks has nearly closed, with strong earnings growth and balance sheets, although growth slows.
Sharp de-rating, Korean memory pricing a 70% cut to 2027 consensus earnings. Highly dependent on AI capex, so volatility stays high.
Lower oil prices are expected to push Energy earnings growth to about -10% in 2027 per consensus. The report lists underweight Energy under the lower inflation and yields theme in several regions.
Selective defensive that has recently re-rated and is exempt from the 2027 growth slowdown, favored in the US, Asia and EM.
Defensive sectors that benefit from lower bond yields.
Beneficiary of the AI capex boom that has re-rated, so exposed to a de-rating if capex slows. Consensus EPS growth roughly halves.
Selective US consumer exposure and European retailers should benefit from lower oil prices and bond yields.
Rate-sensitive areas that benefit if bond yields decline.
Relief in bond markets would hamper their relative performance, though cyclicals have already de-rated against defensives.

earnings_insights: GS top-down 2027 EPS growth forecasts (estimates, not reported): S&P 500 11% vs 36% in 2026, STOXX 600 7% vs about 18%, TOPIX 9% vs 24%, Asia from close to 80% to under 30%. Exhibit 4 shows 2027 EPS growth of 26% for both MSCI AP ex Japan and MSCI EM.

Consensus estimates (not GS) for 2027 EPS growth in Exhibit 7: S&P 500 16.5% vs 32.4% in 2026, STOXX 600 8.4% vs 23.6%, TOPIX 13.2% vs 21.7%, MSCI AP ex Japan 30.0% vs 76.6%, MSCI EM 28.5% vs 77.3%, MSCI AC World 17.0% vs 35.6%.

Consensus sector EPS growth 2026E to 2027E: IT 89.2% to 45.3%, Energy 99.1% to -11.3%, Materials 45.4% to 11.8%, Communication Services 33.7% to -5.2%, Health Care 4.4% to 17.7% (rising), Industrials 22.2% to 13.7%, Financials 12.3% to 9.3%.
Consensus S&P 500 sales growth slows from 12.8% in 2026E to 9.0% in 2027E, with net margin rising from 16.2% to 17.1%.
GS estimates the hyperscaler capex contribution to S&P 500 EPS growth fades through 2027 and 2028 as depreciation charges rise.
For MXAPJ (incl. Korea/Taiwan), GS forecasts EPS growth of 26% in 2027 and 13% in 2028 with a 9.3x target P/E.

Earnings revisions for 2026 and 2027 have been unusually positive, and revisions for 2028 have also increased despite the recent equity sell-off. The strongest upgrades are in EM, driven by Semiconductors.

macro_indicators.reading: About $100/bbl at end-2026 falling to $78/bbl at end-2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: A decline in oil turns the energy-price impulse from a 0.4pp drag on global growth into a modest boost, lowers inflation and supports long-duration Growth and consumers, especially in Europe.

macro_indicators.reading: Brent $88/bbl and WTI $78/bbl, with risks in both directions
macro_indicators.interpretation: Lower energy prices reduce inflation and rate expectations and boost long-duration growth valuations, but cut Energy earnings growth, which weighs more on Europe.

macro_indicators.reading: Move toward rate cuts in late 2027, after a modest tightening cycle and slow progress on cuts
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports modestly lower bond yields. GS rates forecasts are more dovish than market pricing.

macro_indicators.reading: Long-term yields remain elevated, with some relief expected in 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: Relief would favor defensives and long-duration Growth and hamper Cyclicals and Financials. Sovereign debt concerns could still spike yields, with the highest risk in Europe.

macro_indicators.reading: Slows in 2027 as the AI investment boom peaks
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS economists expect slower nominal growth, which is one reason earnings growth halves, though equities usually rise while nominal GDP is growing.

macro_indicators.reading: Expected to widen from current levels
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS credit strategists' view, one reason to prefer selective Defensives with strong balance sheets.
Down from close to the 100th percentile over 20 years. The US remains the most expensive market but is less stretched.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight US Hyperscalers and AI monetisation beneficiaries as long-duration Growth
trade_ideas.rationale: Valuations have fallen to 19.7x P/E, the premium to the rest of the S&P 500 has virtually closed, and balance sheets remain strong.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker AI capex and a faster slowdown in hyperscaler capex growth.

trade_ideas.description: Selective exposure to Korean memory, optical networking, physical AI and Power in Asia
trade_ideas.rationale: Korean memory is pricing a 70% cut to 2027 consensus earnings and trades at 0.7x 2028 P/B, which historically signaled strong forward returns.
trade_ideas.risk: Highly dependent on AI capex, so volatility stays high and concentration risk in Asia is elevated.

trade_ideas.description: Regional allocation: overweight US and Japan, neutral Asia ex Japan and EM, underweight Europe
trade_ideas.rationale: Based on relative growth, profitability and valuation, adjusted for volatility.
trade_ideas.risk: A bond market spike, oil volatility and AI capex shifts could cut either way.

trade_ideas.description: Selective defensives that benefit from lower bond yields: US Healthcare, Power and Buyback Aristocrats, European Telecoms and Utilities, Asian shareholder-return strategies and secure dividends
trade_ideas.rationale: Defensive exposure with reasonable valuations and resilience to slower growth, rather than a broad defensive shift.
trade_ideas.risk: Many traditional Defensives no longer look cheap, so valuation discipline matters.

trade_ideas.description: Beneficiaries of lower oil prices and bond yields: US Consumer Discretionary, European Telecoms, Utilities, UK Real Estate, the DAX and Retailers, plus Transportation, with underweight Energy
trade_ideas.rationale: Lower energy costs strengthen consumers' real incomes and margins outside Energy, and Europe has the greatest imported energy exposure.
trade_ideas.risk: Oil and yields could rise instead, and lower oil cuts European Energy earnings.

risk_factors: Bond market: sovereign debt concerns could spike yields, with the highest risk in Europe during an election-heavy year. Lower yields would instead hamper Cyclicals and Financials.
Oil volatility: forecasts carry risks in both directions. Lower oil would cut Energy earnings growth, which would weigh more on Europe.
Weaker AI capex: an earlier turn in the AI cycle could de-rate memory, chips and parts of Industrials that benefited from the capex boom.
Narrow breadth and momentum concentration in US and Asian indices, with higher risk in Asia.
Credit spreads are expected to widen as growth slows, and borrowing costs remain elevated.
Depreciation charges and interest costs are rising and could pressure earnings.
Tech and AI-related stocks could de-rate further if peak AI capex arrives sooner than expected.
charts_described: Exhibit 12 shows 12m forward P/Es across MSCI AC World sectors and styles: Consumer Staples 21.0x, Consumer Discretionary 20.8x, Hyperscalers 19.7x, EM IT 6.4x, with Hyperscalers cheaper than Consumer Staples.

Exhibit 4 shows 12-month forward return forecasts: S&P 500 7619 to 8700 (14% price), STOXX 600 663 to 700 (6%), TOPIX 3929 to 4500 (15%), MSCI AP ex Japan 819 to 960 (17%), MSCI EM 1576 to 1850 (17%).
Exhibit 7 table of consensus 2026E and 2027E sales growth, EPS growth and net margins by region and sector, for example S&P 500 EPS growth 32.4% to 16.5% and IT 89.2% to 45.3%.
Exhibit 3 shows MSCI AC World 12m forward P/E at 15.6x and the PEG ratio at 1.1, both around their 35-year historical averages.
vol_and_positioning: GS expects positive equity returns in 2027 but with higher volatility than in recent years, and says the range of potential outcomes has widened.
YTD annualised volatility for MXAPJ is 24.2%, the basis for a neutral volatility-adjusted position on Asia ex Japan and EM.
EM index concentration is at a record: Korea and Taiwan are about half of MSCI EM, Info Tech is above 40% and the top 3 stocks (TSMC, Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix) are about 30%.
US and Asia indices are highly concentrated. Narrow breadth raises stock volatility and momentum factor risk, and GS says the risk is higher in Asia than for US large-cap tech.
High dispersion should create a better environment for stock-picking, with a focus on stable earnings, structural growth, strong balance sheets and shareholder returns.
Value has sharply outperformed Growth in all regions in recent months, and the valuation gap between them has narrowed. Cyclicals have de-rated sharply against Defensives.
geopolitical: Some normalisation in the Middle East and a recovery in Persian Gulf supply are expected to reduce geopolitical risk premia and bring down commodity prices, including European gas prices.
Fading US tariff effects are cited as a factor lowering inflation in 2027.
A heavy European political calendar and election-heavy year are cited as risks for Europe, alongside government debt concerns.

tension_points.theme: AI capex peak vs de-rated valuations
tension_points.bull_case: Chip, memory and hyperscaler valuations have fallen sharply, Korean memory prices a 70% cut to 2027 consensus earnings, and hyperscalers retain strong balance sheets and earnings growth, which GS says leaves attractive entry points.
tension_points.bear_case: GS economists expect the AI capex boom to slow, which cuts earnings growth for the AI infrastructure complex and Industrials and could de-rate memory and chips further. Depreciation and interest costs are also rising.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An earlier turn in the AI capex cycle than expected, which the report says would de-rate memory, chips and capex-driven Industrials.

tension_points.bull_case: Lower oil and gas prices support European consumers, lower inflation and rate-sensitive sectors such as Telecoms, Utilities, Retailers and the DAX.
tension_points.bear_case: Lower oil would also cut Energy earnings growth, which matters more for Europe, and Europe's valuations have fallen less than other regions with higher government debt and political risks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further spike in bond yields on sovereign debt concerns, which the report says is most likely in Europe during an election-heavy year.

tension_points.bull_case: Lower bond yields and a late-2027 Fed and ECB easing support long-duration Growth and rate-sensitive sectors.
tension_points.bear_case: Any relief in yields would hamper the relative performance of Cyclicals and Financials, while sovereign debt concerns could instead push yields higher.

theme_stances.key_argument: Hyperscaler capex growth should slow, decelerating earnings growth for the AI infrastructure complex and weakening support for chip names and Industrials.
theme_stances.evidence: growth in AI capex spending is likely to peak

theme_stances.key_argument: Hyperscalers have fallen sharply in P/E, closed the valuation gap with the rest of the S&P 500 and keep strong balance sheets, making them the favored long-duration Growth expression.
On a risk-adjusted basis the US and Japan are favored, Asia and EM neutral and Europe underweight, reflecting growth, profitability and valuation.
theme_stances.evidence: are overweight the US and Japan, neutral in Asia and EM, and underweight Europe
